newsitem.title: MEXICO: Left-winger set for huge Mexico City win -exit poll.
newsitem.headline: Left-winger set for huge Mexico City win -exit poll.

text.p: Leftist opposition veteran Cuauhtemoc Cardenas is set for a landslide victory in Mexico City's first mayoral election, according to an exit poll released after voting ended on Sunday evening.
The poll, by Indemerc/Louis Harris, gave Cardenas 45.77 percent of the vote against 23.3 percent for his nearest rival Alfredo del Mazo of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).
The Indemerc poll said conservative National Action Party (PAN) candidate Carlos Castillo Peraza was trailing the field in third place with 18.56 percent.
The exit poll results were very similar to those given by the last surveys conducted before a pre-election ban took effect on June 28.
The Federal Electoral Institute was due to start releasing preliminary official results from the mayor's race from about 2130 local time (2230 EDT/0230 GMT).
If Cardenas's triumph is confirmed, his victory will be a major blow to the PRI, which had claimed the race would be close.
